mcp_tools.name: correctness_verification_certificate
mcp_tools.title: Correctness verification certificate
mcp_tools.description: Submit a correctness-verification evidence manifest; get a deterministic CERTIFIED / NOT_CERTIFIED / INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE certificate across seven sections (claims register, evidence ladder, specs before tools, evidence artifacts, scope honesty, CI integration, adversarial review and certification) with per-check evidence. One failure breaks the claim.

inputSchema.description: The correctness-verification evidence manifest (see the atom's SERVICE.md for the field table).

component.description: Component whose correctness claim is certified.

register.description: Claims-register evidence (existence, property, scope, evidence level, expiry per claim).

ladder.description: Evidence-ladder evidence (cheapest sufficient level; no claim exceeding its level; tests not presented as proof).

specs.description: Specs-before-tools evidence (invariants, pre/post-conditions, liveness, written before tools ran).

artifacts.description: Evidence-artifact evidence (machine-checkable artifacts, proof scripts/solver logs, counterexamples, reproduction recipe).

scope.description: Scope-honesty evidence (exclusions, versioned claims, re-verification triggers, verified at current version).

ci.description: CI-integration evidence (verification in pipeline; broken proof fails the build).

certificate.description: Certificate evidence (signed attestation binding claim to artifact to commit; independently reproducible).

expect.notes: All 26 boolean checks are satisfied. Computed spot checks: 26/26 checks passed.

checks.evidence: claims register first: one row per claim — no register, no claim
each claim names the property — what exactly is claimed correct
each claim names its scope — which version / configuration the claim covers
each claim carries its evidence level from the ladder
each claim carries an expiry — stale certificates are void
the evidence ladder — L1 static analysis, L2 property-based testing and fuzzing, L3 model checking, L4 deductive verification, L5 proof assistants — cheapest that suffices is selected
no claim exceeds its evidence level (tests are not proof)
tests are not presented as proof — never say proven, bug-free, or certified without property, scope, and evidence
invariants are written in the checker's language
pre- and post-conditions are written in the checker's language
liveness properties are written in the checker's language
specs come before tools: written before running anything
each claim has a machine-checkable artifact behind it
evidence artifacts are retained: counterexamples, proof scripts, solver logs, CI records
never suppress a counterexample
no certificate without a reproduction recipe
what is outside scope is listed — dependencies, hardware, misconfiguration, side channels
every claim is versioned
re-verification triggers are defined — re-verify on change
never certify an artifact that has not been verified at its current version
verification runs in the pipeline
a broken proof fails the build like a broken test
an independent adversarial pass tries to falsify the claim — only unfalsified claims are certified
no counterexample found in adversarial review
a signed attestation binds claim to artifact to source commit (hash and signature)
certificates are signed, versioned, and independently reproducible
